    This document defines performance standards and financial penalties for a benefits administration contractor serving a Department, likely a state employee health program. Key themes include member satisfaction, data reporting, eligibility processing, ID card turnaround, and report timeliness, all governed by measurement criteria and amounts at risk.

Important entities include the Department, Selected Respondent (contractor), Plan Data, Eligibility files, and state employees, including those with disabilities who must have equal access to information. The satisfaction survey (AR-34) requires ≥92% satisfaction, with $50,000 at risk if satisfaction is 90–91.9% and $5,000 more per point below 90%. ID card turnaround requires 99% mailed within four business days, with $10,000 per point below threshold. Plan Data must be delivered monthly, with penalties up to $2,000 per business day late. Eligibility updates require 100% accuracy within two business days; non-routine updates within the same or next business day, each incident risking $2,000 per day.     This knowledge community centers on the contractual obligations, operational responsibilities, and compliance requirements of an “awarded respondent,” likely a health benefits administrator or insurer serving participants, families, and government or agency partners. Key themes include eligibility management, claims processing and adjudication, participant communications, ID card issuance, network and provider billing rules, financial accountability, insurance and bond certification, records retention, and regulatory compliance.

The awarded respondent is the central entity. It maintains the eligibility information system, processes and adjudicates run-out claims, issues checks, collects overpayments, conducts annual other coverage liability verification, and adheres to HIPAA security standards, best industry practices, and GAAP accounting. It communicates expectations, notifies impacted participants 30 days before network status changes, and provides materials for visually impaired participants upon request. It mails ID cards to new participants, individual contracts, and family contracts, typically within ten business days after the open enrollment eligibility file, and provides reports through 16 months following termination.

Relationships emphasize compliance and oversight. The respondent may not overwrite eligibility information without express direction from the Department or People First, must not discuss coverages, and cannot bill participants above allowed amounts. It manages subcontracted services, processes, and deliverables; absorbs benefit-design change and legal defense costs; retains records for ten years; and provides annual bond and insurance certifications. Events of default, including contractor defaults, must be cured within ten calendar days, with payment notice requirements after 45 days.

    This knowledge community centers on a contractual relationship between a public agency and a contractor, with the department acting as overseer. Key themes include contractor obligations, compliance, termination triggers, liability, and confidentiality.

The contractor is an independent contractor, must use E-Verify, maintain background screening and record retention, and provide credit monitoring services. It must answer questions, make good faith efforts, and satisfy obligations to third parties. The contractor maintains a person’s employment file, may request confidentiality agreements with third-party auditors, and claims material as confidential or proprietary.

Significant termination or default triggers include bankruptcy or insolvency proceedings, failure to pay taxes or assessments, failure to provide services, failure to correct rejected work, failure to resume discontinued work, failure to procure or maintain required insurance, and being declared bankrupt. The contractor is responsible for loss of data and liable for reprocurement costs. It must remit a performance guarantee payment to the department within 45 calendar days, give written notice within business days, and notify the department in writing 30 calendar days prior to transfer. It cannot employ persons employed by the state. The contractor must defend lawsuits, assist attorneys, and is not entitled to lost profits or punitive damages. It is subject to a six-year look-back period and must have engaged in business operations in Syria or Cuba. Overall, the agreement emphasizes accountability, compliance, and risk allocation in public contracting.

## Request for Redacted Information

In  the  event  of  a  public  records  or  other  disclosure  request  pursuant  to  Chapter  119, Florida Statutes, the Florida Constitution, or other authority, to which documents that are marked  as  'Confidential'  are  responsive,  the  Department  will  provide  the  Contractorredacted  copies  to  the  requestor.  If  a  requestor  asserts  a  right  to  materials,  which Contractor has identified as confidential, pursuant to section  10.17.2 of this Contract, the Department  will  notify  the  Contractor  such  an  assertion  has  been  made.  It  is  the Contractor's  responsibility  to  assert  that  the  information  in  question  is  exempt  from disclosure under Chapter 119 or other applicable law. If the Department becomes subject to a demand for discovery or disclosure of the Confidential Information of the Contractor under legal process, the Contractor shall be responsible for defending its determination that  the  redacted  portions  of  its  records  are  confidential,  proprietary,  trade  secret,  or otherwise not subject to disclosure.

## Indemnification

The Contractor shall protect, defend, and indemnify the Department for any and all claims arising from or relating to the Contractor's determination that the redacted portions of its records are confidential, proprietary, trade secret, or otherwise not subject to disclosure. If the Contractor fails to submit a redacted copy of information it claims is Confidential, the Department is authorized to produce the entire documents, data, or records submitted to the Department in answer to a public records request or other lawful request for these records.

## Contractor as Agent

Solely for the purposes of this section, the Contract Manager is the agency's custodian of public records. If, under this Contract, the Contractor is providing services and is acting on  behalf  of  a  public  agency,  as  provided  by  section  119.0701,  Florida  Statutes,  the Contractor shall:

- a) Keep and maintain public records required by the public agency to perform the service.

    This document defines performance standards and financial penalties for a benefits administration contractor serving a Department, likely a state employee health program. Key themes include member satisfaction, data reporting, eligibility processing, ID card turnaround, and report timeliness, all governed by measurement criteria and amounts at risk.

Important entities include the Department, Selected Respondent (contractor), Plan Data, Eligibility files, and state employees, including those with disabilities who must have equal access to information. The satisfaction survey (AR-34) requires ≥92% satisfaction, with $50,000 at risk if satisfaction is 90–91.9% and $5,000 more per point below 90%. ID card turnaround requires 99% mailed within four business days, with $10,000 per point below threshold. Plan Data must be delivered monthly, with penalties up to $2,000 per business day late. Eligibility updates require 100% accuracy within two business days; non-routine updates within the same or next business day, each incident risking $2,000 per day. Reports are due weekly or monthly, with $500 per calendar day late.

Relationships show that satisfaction surveys, data submissions, eligibility loads, and report deliveries all connect to measurable deadlines, frequencies, and monetary penalties. The overall context is contractual compliance, emphasizing timely, accurate data exchange and accessible, high-quality member services, with significant financial consequences for nonperformance.

## Disqualifying Offenses

If at any time it is determined that a Person has a criminal misdemeanor or felony record regardless of  adjudication (e.g., adjudication withheld, a plea of guilty or

nolo contendere, or a guilty verdict) within the last six (6) years from the date of the court's determination for the crimes listed below, or their equivalent in any jurisdiction, the Contractor is required to immediately remove that Person from any position with Access to State of Florida Data or directly performing services under the Contract. The disqualifying offenses are:

- (a)  Computer-related crimes;
- (b)  Information technology crimes;
- (c)  Fraudulent practices;
- (d)  False pretenses;
- (e)  Frauds;
- (f) Credit card crimes;
- (g)  Forgery;
- (h)  Counterfeiting;
- (i) Violations involving checks or drafts;
- (j) Misuse of medical or personnel records;
- (k)  Felony theft; and
- (l) Identity Theft.

If the Contractor finds a Disqualifying Offense for a Person within the last six (6) years from the date of the court's disposition, it may obtain information regarding the  incident  and  determine  whether  that  Person  should  continue  providing Services  under  the  Contract  or  have  Access  to  State  of  Florida  Data.  The Contractor will consider the following factors only in making the determination: i.) nature and gravity of the offense, ii.) the amount of time that lapsed since the offense, iii.) the rehabilitation efforts of the person and iv.) relevancy of the offense to the job duties of the Person. If the Contractor determines that the Person should be allowed Access to State of Florida Data, then Contractor shall maintain all criminal background screening information and the rationale for such Access in the Person's employment file.

The Contractor shall require all Persons to self-report within three (3) Business Days of adjudication to the Contractor any adjudication of guilt as described above for  the  Disqualifying  Offenses. The  Contractor  shall  immediately  disallow  that Person Access to any State of Florida Data or from directly performing Services under  the  Contract.    Additionally,  the  Contractor  shall  require  that  the  Person complete an annual certification that he or she has not received an adjudication of guilt  as  described  above  for  the  Disqualifying  Offenses  and  shall  maintain  that certification in the employment file.

## Refresh Screening

The Contractor will ensure that all background screening will be refreshed every five (5) years from the time initially performed for each Person during the term of the Contract.

## Department's Ability to Audit Screening Compliance and Inspect Locations

The Department reserves the right to audit the Contractor's background screening process upon two (2) days prior written Notice to the Contractor during the term of the Contract. Department will have the right to inspect the Contractor's working area, computer systems, and/or location upon two (2) Business Days prior written

notice to the Contractor to ensure that Access to the State of Florida Data is secure and in compliance with the Contract and all applicable state and federal rules and regulations.

## Record Retention

- 2) An entity or affiliate who has been placed on the State's Discriminatory Vendor List may not submit a bid, proposal, or reply on a contract to provide any goods or services to a public entity; may not submit a bid, proposal, or reply on a contract with a public entity for the  construction  or  repair  of  a  public  building  or  public  work;  may  not  submit  bids, proposals, or replies on leases of real property to a public entity; may not be awarded or perform work as a contractor, supplier, subcontractor, or consultant under a contract with any public entity; and may not transact business with any public entity.

Pursuant to sections 287.133, 287.134, and 287.137, Florida Statutes, the following restrictions are placed on the ability of persons placed on the State's Convicted Vendor List,the Discriminatory Vendor List, or the Antitrust Violator Vendor List:

- 1) A person or affiliate who has been placed on the State's Convicted Vendor List following a conviction for a public entity crime may not submit a bid, proposal, or reply on a contract to provide any goods or services to a public entity; may not submit a bid, proposal, or reply on a contract with a public entity for the construction or repair of a public building or public work; may not submit bids, proposals, or replies on leases of real property to a public entity; may  not  be  awarded  or  perform  work  as  a  contractor,  supplier, subcontractor, or consultant under a contract with any public entity; and may not transact business with any public entity in excess of the threshold amount provided in section 287.017,  Florida  Statute,  for  CATEGORY  TWO  for  a  period  of  thirty-six  (36)  months following the date of being placed on the State's Convicted Vendor List.

- 3) A  person  or  an  affiliate  who  has  been  placed  on  the  Antitrust  Violator  Vendor  List following a conviction or being held civilly liable for an antitrust violation may not submit a bid, proposal, or reply for any new contract to provide any goods or services to a public entity; may not submit a bid, proposal, or reply for a new contract with a public entity for the  construction  or  repair  of  a  public  building  or  public  work;  may  not  submit  a  bid, proposal, or reply on new leases of real property to a public entity; may not be awarded or  perform  work  as  a  contractor,  supplier,  subcontractor,  or  consultant  under  a  new contract with a public entity; and may not transact new business with a public entity.
